_comment: IRN OS app manifest — the single declaration of which companion apps ship in
the image, where their source lives, how each one is built, and what each one
talks to on the network.
WHY A MANIFEST AND NOT A PILE OF SHELL SCRIPTS: the stager, the chroot hook,
the irn-app launcher, the app store and the desktop menu all need the same
handful of facts about each app. When those facts live in five places they
drift, and the way you find out is that an app is in the menu with a launcher
that points at a directory the stager never copied. Declared once here,
enforced by src/os/appManifest.test.js, consumed by everything else. This is
the same shape as src/irnl/spec/irn.irn: declare once, enforce by tests.
THE FIELD THAT MATTERS MOST IS `network`. IRN's whole premise is that client
data does not leave the device. An app store that silently ships a cloud app
next to a local-only one launders that distinction away. So every entry states
what it sends and to whom, and the conformance test cross-checks that claim
against the app's real dependency list on disk — you cannot quietly add
@supabase or googleapis to an app and keep `network.required: false`.
JSON HAS NO COMMENTS, so the WHY lives in `_comment` arrays. Any key starting
with an underscore is documentation and is ignored by every consumer.
Adding an app? Read os/apps/README.md. Do not hand-edit an entry to make the
test pass — if the test is unhappy, the image is about to be wrong.

apps.name: EquityGuard
apps.summary: Local-first ledger for logging discrimination incidents and reviewing the running tally. Keeps everything in the browser profile; nothing is posted anywhere.

network.note: No egress. src/routes/+page.server.js carries the comment 'Technical Incapacity loader. DO NOT wire this to any database.' and returns empty arrays; +layout.js sets prerender = true, so adapter-static emits a fully prerendered bundle with no server half.

_comment: BUILD IS ALREADY CORRECT: svelte.config.js uses @sveltejs/adapter-static
with pages/assets both 'build' and strict:true, and the root +layout.js
declares prerender = true. `npx vite build` produces build/ = 104K.
NO ICON ASSET EXISTS. There is no static/ directory in this project at all,
so there is nothing to copy. The icon is a stock name from the freedesktop
Icon Naming Specification, which every compliant theme resolves — that is
the only kind of bare name allowed here (see README, 'Icons').

apps.name: EquityGuard Witness
apps.summary: Firefox extension that flags and counts discriminatory patterns on pages you are already reading, and hands what it finds to the EquityGuard ledger. Counts live in extension storage.

network.note: Zero egress: grep for fetch( / XMLHttpRequest / http:// / https:// across every .js and .html in the tree returns nothing. Its only permission is 'storage'. It DOES inject content.js into <all_urls> and a bridge.js into localhost, 127.0.0.1 and equityguard.netlify.app — broad injection, but read-only and offline.

_comment: NO BUILD STEP AND NO dist: this is a hand-written MV3 extension, 28K of
loose files. The hook copies the directory as-is into the Firefox extension
path; there is nothing to compile.
launch IS null ON PURPOSE. A webext has no process of its own and no
.desktop entry — Firefox owns it. The store lists it so an operator knows
it is installed and what it does; the menu WP must skip type webext rather
than invent a launcher for it.
manifest.json HAS NO `icons` KEY (verified: the top-level keys are exactly
manifest_version, name, version, permissions, action, background,
content_scripts). Firefox will draw its default puzzle-piece in the toolbar.
The `icon` below is for the IRN store listing only, not for the browser.
ext_id is invented here rather than read from the source — the extension
declares no browser_specific_settings.gecko.id. Firefox needs a stable id
to install an unsigned extension from a policy, so the hook WP must write
this id into the staged manifest.json. If that id ever changes, the
already-installed copy on an existing box becomes a second extension.

apps.name: School Not Prison
apps.summary: The School ≠ Prison Pipeline campaign site — the argument, the numbers, the stories, and the petition. Read-only reference copy for offline organizing.

network.note: The shipped bundle is fully prerendered and offline: no server half, no fetch to any host. The one outbound call in the source is the petition form POSTing to its own origin at /api/petition, and that endpoint is deliberately not built — see _comment, because it is a UX problem rather than an egress one.

_comment: WORK PACKAGE U HAS LANDED, and it took three separate changes rather than
the one 'switch the adapter' the audit implied. Recorded because the next
SvelteKit app added to this manifest will hit the same three:
1. The adapter is now @sveltejs/adapter-static, was @sveltejs/adapter-auto.
adapter-auto resolves to a hosting provider at build time and produces
nothing usable off-platform.
2. WHERE THE ADAPTER LIVES. There is NO svelte.config.js in this project —
the adapter is imported and set inline in vite.config.ts (line 1, and
`adapter: adapter()` at line 19). Anyone who goes looking for
svelte.config.js and creates one ends up with two competing configs.
3. PRERENDERING. adapter-static with no prerendered pages and no fallback
fails the build outright, and there was no `export const prerender` in
src/ at all. A root src/routes/+layout.ts now declares prerender = true.
`npx vite build` now produces build/ = 856K (index.html, _app/, robots.txt).
THE PETITION FORM IS THE OPEN ITEM, and it is not a build detail.
src/routes/api/petition/+server.ts was a POST handler collecting firstName,
lastName, email, zip and phone. A POST endpoint cannot be prerendered, so WP
U parked it as api/petition/server.stub.ts — SvelteKit only routes files
named +server.ts, so the endpoint is now correctly absent from the static
build. That is the right call for an offline image.
But src/lib/components/PetitionForm.svelte:27 still POSTs to /api/petition,
so in the shipped bundle the form renders, collects a supporter's name,
email, zip and phone, and hits a 404. The failure is at least honest — the
catch sets 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' rather than showing the
'Your name has been added.' success panel — so nobody is told their
signature was recorded when it was not, and no data goes anywhere. It is
still a form in a shipped app that can never succeed. The offline build
should hide it and point at how to sign for real.
AND IF IT EVER GAINS A DESTINATION, THIS ENTRY'S network BLOCK STOPS BEING
TRUE. The stub still carries a commented-out Supabase insert as its TODO.
Wiring that up would make this app collect names, emails and phone numbers
and send them to a third party — `sends: casework`, at which point it needs
the same treatment as IRN OS Console, not a quiet edit to +server.ts.

apps.name: SoulCoin Wallet
apps.summary: Wallet interface for SoulCoin, a Taproot Assets token. Talks only to a Taproot Assets daemon you run yourself on this machine.

network.note: Only the static bundle ships, so there is no egress at all. Even the relay that is NOT shipped points at localhost: server.js:15 reads `TAPD_REST_URL || 'https://localhost:8089'`, a Taproot Assets daemon on this host. No cloud endpoint appears anywhere in the tree.

_comment: SHIP THE STATIC BUNDLE ONLY. `npx vite build` produces dist/ = 264K.
server.js IS DELIBERATELY IN `exclude`. It is an Express relay (express,
cors, axios, dotenv) that proxies wallet calls to a local tapd. Nobody
running IRN OS off a USB stick has a Taproot Assets daemon on 8089, so the
relay would sit there doing nothing but listening — a port open for a
service that cannot work. If a real tapd deployment ever needs it, promote
this entry to node-service and re-declare `network` then, because at that
point the app genuinely does talk to something.
This is the only app in the roster shipping its own icon file from the
source tree rather than a stock freedesktop name: public/favicon.svg.

apps.name: IRN Launchpad
apps.summary: Hub for IRN's internal modules — pick a module and it opens. Runs entirely on this machine as a local server.

network.note: Serves itself from 127.0.0.1 and talks to nothing else. As of the WP U cleanup there is no cloud SDK in package.json at all — the dependency list is next, react, framer-motion, lucide-react, clsx, tailwind-merge and a TypeScript/Tailwind toolchain. The conformance test re-reads that list on every run.

_comment: WHY node-service AND NOT web-static: src/app/modules/[module]/page.tsx is a
dynamic route rendered by the server on demand. There is no finite set of
module slugs to prerender, so a static export drops every module page and
leaves a hub whose links all 404. It needs a Node process.
WORK PACKAGE U HAS LANDED. next.config.ts now sets output: 'standalone' and
`npm run build` produces .next/standalone = 36M containing server.js,
package.json and a pruned node_modules. That is why the 511M top-level
node_modules is excluded — standalone already carries what the server needs.
WP U also had to pin `outputFileTracingRoot` to the project directory:
without it Next walks upward, finds a stray lockfile in $HOME, and nests the
output at .next/standalone/Dev/web/irn-launchpad/, which would leave the
stager looking at an empty directory.
THIS ENTRY USED TO CARRY dep_exceptions FOR @supabase/ssr AND
@supabase/supabase-js, and the record of why is worth keeping. They were
installed but dead — grep for '@supabase' across src/ returned zero hits.
The exceptions were written to be self-expiring: the conformance test
requires an exempted package to still be present on disk, so when WP U
removed the dependencies the suite went red on a stale exception and forced
the block to be deleted. That is exactly what happened, minutes after the
entry was written. The mechanism is not theoretical.
NOTHING GUARDS THIS ENTRY NOW EXCEPT THE CROSS-CHECK ITSELF, which is the
correct end state: with no exception block, the moment any of @supabase/*,
googleapis, @notionhq/, @google/generative-ai, openai or @anthropic-ai/
reappears in package.json, the egress test fails on this app and demands
either an honest network declaration or a justified exception. Do not add a
blanket exception to quiet it.
PORT COLLISION: `next start` defaults to 3000, and so does Sovereign
Hivemind. Two of the ten apps want the same port. The launcher WP must
assign ports rather than let both take the default.

apps.name: IRN OS Console
apps.summary: Multi-provider AI console wired to IRN's back office. THIS APP SENDS DATA TO THIRD-PARTY CLOUD SERVICES — it is the one app here that is not local-first.

network.note: Verified egress, not inferred. server/supabase.js:1 createClient from @supabase/supabase-js; server/server.js:6 imports googleapis and :7 @notionhq/client; server/providers.js:37 POSTs prompts to generativelanguage.googleapis.com; server/server.js:601 queries www.googleapis.com/customsearch/v1. The client also <link>s fonts.googleapis.com from client/index.html:8 and :10, so even loading the UI announces the machine to Google before a single request is made. Backend listens on 4567 (server/server.js:1181).

_comment: THIS IS THE EXCEPTION IN THE ROSTER AND IT IS LABELLED AS ONE. Everything
else here is local-first; this one is a real cloud client. It is not being
smuggled in — `sends: casework` and a four-entry `services` list are exactly
how it should read, so the store can put a warning on it and an operator can
make an informed choice. If a future edit ever quietly flips
network.required to false, the conformance test catches it: @supabase/*,
googleapis and @notionhq/client are all in package.json and there is no
dep_exceptions block here.
THE FONT LINK IS PART OF THE EGRESS. client/index.html pulls Outfit and
JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com. Both fonts are already in the
image (fonts-jetbrains-mono is in the package list), so self-hosting them
would remove one whole class of beacon for near-zero effort. Worth doing
even though it does not change this entry's declaration.
NO AUTOSTART, AND THE TEST ENFORCES IT. An app that phones four cloud
services must never come up on its own at login — the operator starts it
deliberately or it does not run.
SIZE: node_modules is 327M and the server genuinely needs it at runtime
(express, googleapis, @notionhq/client, @supabase/supabase-js), so it is
NOT excluded — only its cache is. That is a third of a gigabyte for one
app; the stager WP may prefer `npm ci --omit=dev` in the hook instead, but
that trades image size for a build that needs network.
dist/ IS 2.6M, NOT THE ~289K THE BUILDABILITY AUDIT RECORDED. The delta is
one file: dist/irn-crest.png is 2,353,931 bytes. The JS/CSS bundle really is
~296K. The crest is a 2.3M PNG being used as an app icon, which is absurd
for something drawn at 48px — downscaling it would recover 2.3M of squashfs.
`client/dist` is excluded because it is a stale duplicate of the same build;
vite.config.js sets build.outDir to '../dist', so the top-level dist/ is the
real output and client/dist/ is left over from an earlier configuration.

apps.name: Sovereign Hivemind
apps.summary: Peer-to-peer intelligence node: discovers other nodes over local mDNS and embeds documents with a local Ollama model. No coordinator, no account, nothing off the LAN.

dep_exceptions.reason: Dormant. Imported only by ghost_bridge.ts:1, a TypeScript file in a CommonJS project (package.json type: commonjs) with no build step and no compiled .js counterpart. Nothing in cli.js, index.js, hivemind.js or network.js references ghost_bridge at all, so the code path cannot be reached from the shipped entry point. Ships as dead weight, not as egress. If a TypeScript build is ever added to this project, delete this exception and re-audit — the import becomes live the moment it can be required.

network.note: LAN and localhost only. network.js:4 uses multicast-dns and advertises/queries sovereign-hivemind.local (lines 103, 111, 153) — link-local, never leaves the subnet. Embeddings go to http://localhost:11434 (index.js:136, hivemind.js:44), the Ollama already in this image. sends is 'queries' rather than 'none' because document text does go over the wire to peers on the LAN; it just never reaches the internet.

_comment: THE ONE THING YOU MUST NOT GET WRONG HERE:
local_vector_db.json IS 1,007,629,647 BYTES — one gigabyte of runtime
embedding data sitting in the project directory. Staging it would add ~1G to
a live ISO to ship one machine's accumulated vectors to every other machine.
It is regenerated from whatever the operator ingests, so a fresh install
wants it empty anyway. It is first in `exclude` for a reason, and the
conformance test refuses to let `exclude` be dropped or emptied.
THERE IS ALSO A .env IN THIS TREE. Its contents were not read and must not
be: an .env in a project that imports @google/generative-ai is a credential
until proven otherwise, and credentials do not go into a squashfs that ships
to other people. Excluded.
sanctuary_state.json is 128 bytes of this box's runtime state. Small, but
still one machine's state being cloned onto every other machine.
package.json DECLARES NO `bin`. The `hivemind` name is chosen here, and the
hook WP has to generate the wrapper (node /opt/irn-apps/hivemind/cli.js).
There is no upstream binary to symlink to.
node_modules IS NOT EXCLUDED (37M). Unlike the web apps, a node-cli needs
its dependencies present at runtime and the image build has no network to
fetch them with. Only the cache is dropped.
PORT COLLISION: cli.js:4 reads `process.env.PORT || 3000`, the same default
IRN Launchpad's `next start` takes. On a box running both, whichever starts
second fails to bind. The launcher WP must set PORT explicitly.

apps.name: IRN CLI
apps.summary: IRN's command line: chat with a local model, build case context, dispatch tasks, and fact-check claims against a local verified-facts database.

network.note: Offline by default. `chat` uses the local Ollama. The single off-device path is `facts verify`, and it is doubly gated: it needs BOTH the --live flag and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the operator set themselves (src/commands/facts.js:177 and :192). With no key, src/lib/factcheck/deepverify.js:102 refuses with a message that names itself as 'the only command in this tool that sends claim text off-device' before src/lib/factcheck/deepverify.js:116 could ever reach api.anthropic.com. The image ships no key, so the path is closed unless an operator opens it on purpose.

_comment: sends IS 'queries', NOT 'none'. There is no key in the image and no way to
reach Anthropic without one, so in practice this ships offline — but the
code to send claim text off-device is present and one environment variable
away. Declaring 'none' would be a claim about the operator's future
configuration, not about this binary. When the honest answer and the
flattering answer differ, the manifest takes the honest one.
The `facts` implementation lives here, in src/commands/facts.js. See the
`excluded` block below for ~/Dev/tools/fact-check, which is a second,
unmerged copy of the same idea and is NOT shipped.
node_modules (7.7M) is not excluded — same reason as Hivemind.

apps.name: Hermes Agent
apps.summary: Developer-tooling CLI with a small pluggable skill system: list, run and manage skills, generate images locally, and run sandboxed shell commands.

network.note: No egress. grep across src/hermes for requests, urllib, http://, https://, anthropic and openai returns nothing — despite the project describing itself as an 'AI-enhanced' CLI, there is no network client in it. `image_gen` renders locally.

_comment: WORK PACKAGE U HAS LANDED on pyproject.toml. The authors entry used to be
`{ name = "Aziza Team", email = "aziza@localhost" }`; modern setuptools
validates that address and a bare hostname with no dot fails, which broke
`pip install .` before anything else could go wrong. The email field is now
dropped entirely rather than replaced with a real address — a package that
is only ever installed locally does not need a contact address, and putting
one in a file that ships on a USB stick to strangers is a choice, not a fix.
DEBIAN PACKAGES, NOT PIP. Dependencies are click and pyyaml, both of which
Debian ships as python3-click and python3-yaml. Adding them to the package
list means the image needs no network at build time and no per-app venv —
the same call stage-extras.sh already makes for Sanctuary Terminal, which
uses Debian's python3-pyqt5 rather than a venv built against another
distro's Python. `deb_deps` is what the package-list WP reads.
VERIFIED RUNNING, not assumed: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m hermes.cli --help`
exits 0 and prints its five commands (computer_use, image_gen, list, manage,
run). The PYTHONPATH matters — packages live under src/, so the wrapper the
hook generates must either set PYTHONPATH or install the package properly.
ONE COMMAND DESERVES A SECOND LOOK BEFORE SHIP: `computer_use` is described
as 'Execute safe sandboxed shell command'. A command that calls itself
sandboxed is a claim to verify, not to accept — see the Zee Zee
sandbox_runner finding for how that has gone before.

apps.name: QuantumNeuralVM
apps.summary: Demonstration harness for a quantum-circuit simulator. Reports benchmark timings for GHZ-state circuits. See the note — the simulator core is a stub and its headline numbers are hardcoded.

network.note: No egress. Pure local computation over numpy/scipy/psutil.

_comment: requirements.txt IS MISLEADING AND MUST BE IGNORED. It lists pytest, sphinx,
black and coverage — a developer's toolchain, not the app's dependencies.
The real runtime dependencies are in setup.py install_requires: numpy>=1.24,
scipy>=1.11, psutil>=5.9. All three are in Debian, hence `deb_deps`.
THE HEADLINE NUMBERS ARE HARDCODED. The buildability audit recorded this app
as 'Verified running: Success True, Fidelity 0.9954'. Running it here does
not reproduce that, because those values are not computed:
src/qnvm/qnvm_wrapper.py:30   'success': True,
src/qnvm/qnvm_wrapper.py:32   'estimated_fidelity': 0.9954
are literals in a returned dict, and quantum_processor.py:30 likewise
returns `0.99  # Demo fidelity`. The simulator itself is a stub:
advanced_quantum_simulator.py:42 is docstringed 'Simplified simulator for
demonstration' and simulate_ghz_circuit builds `{'method', 'num_qubits'}`
under a `# Demo simulation` comment without touching the H and X matrices it
defined. A real 16-qubit run returns memory_used_gb 0.0 in 0.23ms and no
fidelity field at all — which is what you would expect from code that
simulates nothing.
SO: this is a demo, and the summary says so. It is recorded here because
IRN's docs are load-bearing for grants and credibility; a stub billed in an
app store as a working quantum VM is exactly the kind of claim that costs
more than it earns. Aziza's call whether it ships at all — moving it to the
`excluded` block below is a one-line change and would not be a loss.
THE DECLARED CONSOLE SCRIPT IS BROKEN TWO WAYS, so `entry` is the module
invocation and NOT setup.py's console_scripts:
1. setup.py declares `qnvm-benchmark = benchmarks.run_ghz_benchmark:...`
while `packages=find_packages(where='src')` — benchmarks/ is outside
src/, so pip never installs it and the generated script cannot import
its own target.
2. Console scripts are invoked with zero arguments, but
run_ghz_benchmark(qubits, ...) has no default for qubits, so it would
raise TypeError on the first call.
`python -m benchmarks.run_ghz_benchmark` works instead: the module has an
argparse __main__ block that defaults to 16 qubits. The hook WP must
generate the qnvm-benchmark wrapper around the module invocation.
THE DEFAULT OUTPUT PATH DOES NOT SURVIVE A READ-ONLY IMAGE. output_dir
defaults to the relative path 'benchmarks/results', so the tool writes into
its own install directory. Under /opt in a squashfs that is an immediate
OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system — observed, not predicted. The
wrapper must pass an output directory under $HOME.
venv/ IS 316M OF THE 317M TREE. Excluded for the same reason
stage-extras.sh refuses to copy Sanctuary Terminal's .venv: it is built
against another distro's Python and points at an interpreter that will not
exist in the image. Without it this app is about 1M.

apps.name: Sanctuary Terminal
apps.summary: The IRN terminal: split panes and tabs, a redaction mode that masks PII on screen, find-in-scrollback, OSC 133 shell integration, and a two-tier panic that blanks the screen before it burns the session.

network.note: One egress path, opt-in twice. The terminal itself is offline — it forks a shell and draws bytes. sanctuary_term.py:3651 antigravity_selection() writes `agy -p <selection>` into the live shell, and agy is Google's Antigravity agent. It refuses unless redaction mode is ON (sanctuary_term.py:3653, default-closed via getattr, so a terminal that has never toggled redaction is blocked), and the selection goes through redact_text() at :3666 before it leaves, masking SSN/DOB/MRN/docket/email/phone/card patterns, then through shlex.quote at :3668 so displayed output cannot become a second command. Regex redaction does NOT mask names or narrative prose, so client-derived text can still reach a third party — that is why this is 'casework' and not 'queries'. Pinned by tests/test_view.py::TestAntigravityGate in the terminal's own repo (6 tests, each mutation-checked). required is false because the terminal needs no network to do its job, and the image ships no agy binary, so the path is inert until an operator installs one.

_comment: TYPE python-gui EXISTS FOR THIS APP. A PyQt5 window is neither a web-static
bundle nor a CLI: filed as python-cli it would inherit Terminal=true and
the menu entry would open a terminal inside a terminal. See os/apps/README.md.
CATEGORIES ARE Utility;TerminalEmulator; AND NOT System;. TerminalEmulator
is an additional category that needs exactly one main category beside
it. Utility and System are both main categories, and an entry with two
of them can appear twice in the menu. This was learned once already, in
the hand-written .desktop file this entry replaces.
IT USED TO BE STAGED BY os/stage-extras.sh, which copied an allowlist of
seven files into /opt/sanctuary-terminal and wrote its own .desktop entry.
That path is removed: it hardcoded $HOME/vault/Desktop/Folders/Sanctuary/
terminal, the project moved to ~/vault/Sanctuary/terminal, and the script
then exited 1 before it reached Zee Zee or Ollama. A src path declared in
one place that five consumers read is the whole reason this manifest exists.
THE EGRESS CROSS-CHECK CANNOT SEE THIS APP. Block 5 of the conformance test
reads package.json, and this is Python with no package.json, so the network
block above is a declaration nothing automated verifies. It was checked by
hand against the source at the line numbers named in the note.
.venv IS EXCLUDED and must stay excluded: it is built against Garuda's
Python and points at an interpreter that does not exist in the image. The
deb_deps above are what the app actually runs on in Debian trixie.

excluded.name: IRN Fact Check
excluded.reason: Not an app — an unmerged duplicate of code irn-cli already ships.
_comment: Its own package.json describes it as a 'Fact-check drop-in for irn-cli', and
that is literally what it is: main points at src/commands/facts.js, which
exports registerFactsCommand(program) and expects a host CLI to hand it a
commander instance. There is no `bin` field, no program.parse() call and no
entry point — running --help exits 0 and prints nothing, which is what a
library looks like when you try to run it as a program.
Meanwhile irn-cli already has its own separate `facts` implementation at
src/commands/facts.js in its own tree. Shipping this would install a second
copy of the same feature that cannot be invoked. Whether the two
implementations should be reconciled upstream is a real question, but it is
not one the OS image gets to answer.

excluded.name: inir
excluded.reason: Arch-only desktop shell. Neither of its two hard requirements exists in Debian trixie.
_comment: inir is a Quickshell configuration for the Niri compositor — .qml files, a
settings shell, panels and overlays. IRN OS runs labwc, and more to the
point Debian trixie packages neither `niri` nor `quickshell`, so there is
nothing for this configuration to configure.
Its `setup` script confirms the platform assumption: it stages AUR builds
through yay/paru (setup:12 and :36 clean up /tmp/buildyay and /tmp/buildparu).
An AUR helper on a Debian image is a category error, not a missing package.
Porting is a from-scratch job: build Niri and Quickshell for Debian, then
re-test the configuration against them. That is its own project. Note also
that a second compositor would compete with labwc for the session, so this
would be a replacement for the desktop, not an addition to the app menu.

excluded.name: Cardputer Ember
excluded.reason: Embedded firmware, not desktop software. Belongs in a flashing tool.
_comment: This is a PlatformIO project (platformio.ini + src/) targeting the ESP32 in
an M5Cardputer with a LoRa radio — the mutual-aid mesh terminal. It compiles
to a binary that runs on the handheld, not on the machine booting this
image. There is no window to open and no command to run.
It is not being dropped, it is being routed elsewhere: the right home is a
flashing/provisioning tool in the image (esptool plus the prebuilt firmware),
so an organizer can flash a Cardputer from an IRN OS box. That is a separate
work package with a different shape — a device workflow, not an app entry.
See the Cardputer Ember memory for the build and download-mode gotchas.
Listing it here rather than silently omitting it is the point of this block:
the next person to inventory ~/ will find it, wonder why it is not in the
menu, and get the answer without repeating the investigation.
